name: Read the benchmark claim critically
note: Each line is a real-sounding benchmark claim. Pick the single sharpest reason to distrust it before you act on it.

items.prompt: Our model scores 95% on a popular benchmark first published in 2021. Its training data runs through 2024.
candidates: Contamination — the public test set was almost certainly in the training data
items.correct: Contamination — the public test set was almost certainly in the training data
items.explanation: A public benchmark older than the training cutoff has likely leaked into pretraining, so a high score can measure memorization, not capability. Check for it with held-out or post-cutoff variants (LiveBench), canary strings, or perturbed questions.
items.principle: A public benchmark inside the training data measures recall, not skill.

items.prompt: Three frontier models score 89–90% on MMLU; ours hits 90.3% — a new state of the art.
candidates: Saturation — near the ceiling, 0.3 points is within noise, not a real gap
They used the wrong prompt format
items.correct: Saturation — near the ceiling, 0.3 points is within noise, not a real gap
items.explanation: Once a benchmark saturates, the remaining headroom is label noise and ambiguous items. A 0.3-point 'SOTA' there is meaningless without a confidence interval (Chapter 3) — and probably even with one. Move to a harder or fresher benchmark.
items.principle: Near a benchmark's ceiling, ranking is noise; switch benchmarks before you switch models.

items.prompt: Our model tops the HumanEval coding leaderboard, so it's the best choice for our large production codebase.
candidates: Construct validity — short self-contained puzzles don't resemble a real codebase
The score wasn't averaged over runs
items.correct: Construct validity — short self-contained puzzles don't resemble a real codebase
items.explanation: HumanEval is 164 small, self-contained function-completion problems; production work is multi-file, repo-context-heavy edits. SWE-bench (real GitHub issues) is the far closer proxy. A benchmark can be valid and still measure the wrong construct for your use.
items.principle: Ask what a benchmark actually measures before trusting it for a different task.
